newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks seen likely to fall, then recover.
newsitem.headline: China stocks seen likely to fall, then recover.

text.p: China's share markets are likely to see a sharp reaction from investors to mark the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, but many people will be waiting eagerly to buy into any significant falls, brokers said on Thursday.
John Crossman, Shanghai representative for Jardine Fleming, predicted the China B share market could be down five percent or more initially but could end the day up as much as two percent.
"I think we'll see a sharp reaction down from locals, but there are foreigners who have been waiting for this buying opportunity for quite a while," he said.
"I think money's going to go into the market, so there's a very good chance of down in the morning and up in the afternoon," he added.
A Chinese broker said he expected a sharp fall on very small volume initially but said there was a strong possibility of a quick rebound.
Other Chinese brokers in both Shanghai and Shenzhen said they saw a strong possibility of two or three days of 10 percent limit-down falls on the local currency A share markets.
But two said they expected the government to order major brokerages to step in and support markets for several days to offset a large part of any selling pressure.
"The main concern is political instability," said a broker in Shenzhen. "People will be watching to see what measures the government takes over the next few days."

A local broker in Shanghai said the Chinese stock markets, set up in 1990, had already gained a measure of maturity, and would probably at most fall about as much as they did in their last major correction in mid-December.
Stock prices fell around 30 percent at that time after Beijing warned the markets that they were becoming over-heated.
"But if the Hong Kong markets and the B shares drop sharply there could be a much bigger reaction on the A share markets," said one broker.

"The market is definitely going to fall," said a third broker. "There is the strong possibility of the markets hitting 10 percent limit-down for two or three days. But if there is no sign of serious instability, the market can recover by the middle of next week."
